gap: No result ChatGPT got that I could read states that VIA's own supported-keyboards list ("Compatible as of 9/19/2026") has no Lofree, NuPhy or Keychron K7 entry, so the Lofree Flow 2's "VIA remapping" only works after loading Lofree's JSON definition file by hand (Digital Trends' Paulo Vargas: "VIA wouldn't properly recognize the keyboard without it").
standout_why: Compared against keebscout's low-profile guide and mkbguide's low-profile and 65% guides, which I read in full; none mentions the VIA definition file. The four RTINGS pages (best low-profile, Flow 2 review, Air75 V3 review, the comparison) returned only a navigation shell, so I could not check whether the cited Flow 2 review already covers the VIA step; that is why this is 1 and not 2. My first candidate mechanism, that each low-profile hot-swap socket takes one switch family, is already on rival pages: mkbguide says hot-swap "very rarely means you can drop in any low-profile switch you like" and "NuPhy's V3 boards take the LP 3.0 Nano generation"; keebscout says the "three ecosystems ... do not mix". All three maker stores (lofree.co, nuphy.com, keychron.com) returned HTTP 429 on every attempt, so nothing here is in the makers' own words.
decides: It does not change the pick; it qualifies the Lofree Flow 2 68 row. A shopper choosing the Flow 2 68 for remapping should know VIA will not detect it until Lofree's JSON file is loaded, and that Vargas found the Fn key could not be remapped (on the 84-key Mac version; no Flow 2 68 review was found). For switch swaps, the three candidates are separate ecosystems per the rival pages, so spare switches from one will not carry to another.
